new_value: • Historical reckoning dates for the eras: Vikrama era began in 58 B.C. (traditionally associated with King Vikramaditya of Ujjain); Saka era began in 78 A.D. (initiated by Kushana King Kanishka); Gupta era was established in 319-320 A.D. by Chandragupta I; and Kali era traditionally commences from 3102 B.C. (the Aihole inscription date). Therefore, the correct combination is I-D, II-C, III-B, IV-A. • Why Option A is incorrect: Assigns 320 A.D. (Gupta era) to Vikrama era, 58 B.C. to Saka era, and 248 A.D. (Kalachuri-Chedi era) to Gupta era. • Why Option B is incorrect: Assigns 3102 B.C. to Vikrama era and 58 B.C. to Kali era. • Why Option C is incorrect: Mistakenly pairs the Saka era with 248 A.D. (Kalachuri era) and Kali era with 78 A.D. (Saka era). • Often confused with: The Vikrama era (58 B.C.) and Saka era (78 A.D.) are frequently swapped. Remember that Vikrama is B.C. (pre-Christian era) while Saka is A.D. (the basis of India's National Civil Calendar). Also note that 248 A.D. (Option E) marks the Kalachuri/Traikutaka era, included here as a distractor.
issues_found: No pre-existing explanation was provided in the prompt to critique, so standard historical dates and alignments were derived directly from classical Indian epigraphy (e.g., Aihole inscription, Kanishka's accession, Chandragupta I's coronation).
